---
title: "Battlegrounds: what the polls missed"
subtitle: "Selected 2026 Senate contests · results and polling errors"
description: "Verified Senate outcomes and dated polling-error estimates for eight battleground states."
---

This page replaces pre-election scenarios with reported 2026 outcomes. Where public sources do not provide comparable final vote shares or race-level spending figures, those values are omitted rather than estimated.

## Polling error by state

Pew Research Center compared the final Democratic-minus-Republican polling average with unofficial vote counts as of Nov. 11, 2026. A positive value means the polls understated the Democratic margin. These are **signed polling errors**, not the candidates' actual vote margins or poll averages.

```{r}
#| label: polling-error
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

poll_error <- tribble(
  ~state, ~error,
  "Texas", 8.9,
  "Georgia", 8.9,
  "North Carolina", 8.5,
  "New Hampshire", 5.4,
  "Florida", 3.3,
  "Maine", 2.1,
  "Ohio", 2.0,
  "Michigan", 1.8
) |>
  mutate(
    state = fct_reorder(state, error),
    hover = paste0(state, "<br>Polling error: +", error,
                   " points<br>Polls understated the Democratic margin")
  )

poll_error_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = poll_error,
  x = ~error,
  y = ~state,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(size = 13, color = "#1d4ed8", line = list(color = "white", width = 1)),
  text = ~hover,
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  add_segments(
    x = 0, xend = ~error, y = ~state, yend = ~state,
    inherit = FALSE,
    line = list(color = "#94a3b8", width = 3),
    showlegend = FALSE,
    hoverinfo = "skip"
  ) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "Polling error (percentage points)", rangemode = "tozero"),
    yaxis = list(title = NULL),
    margin = list(l = 125, t = 20, b = 55),
    annotations = list(
      list(x = 0, y = 1.08, xref = "x", yref = "paper",
           text = "0 = no polling error", showarrow = FALSE,
           xanchor = "left", font = list(size = 11, color = "#64748b"))
    )
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

poll_error_plot
```

::: {.source-note}
Source: [Pew Research Center, “A First Look at Polling Performance in 2026”](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/11/12/a-first-look-at-polling-performance-in-2026/), updated Nov. 12. The results used in its calculations were unofficial counts available Nov. 11; some races were not final.
:::

## How the selected Senate outcomes break down by region

The eight states below are a selected set, not every competitive Senate contest. The chart counts reported winners by party; it does not represent vote share or regional vote swing.

```{r}
#| label: regional-results
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

regional_results <- tribble(
  ~state, ~region, ~winner_party,
  "Maine", "Northeast", "Democratic",
  "New Hampshire", "Northeast", "Democratic",
  "Michigan", "Rust Belt", "Democratic",
  "Ohio", "Rust Belt", "Democratic",
  "North Carolina", "Sun Belt", "Democratic",
  "Georgia", "Sun Belt", "Democratic",
  "Texas", "Sun Belt", "Democratic",
  "Florida", "Sun Belt", "Republican"
) |>
  count(region, winner_party, name = "races") |>
  complete(region, winner_party, fill = list(races = 0)) |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region, levels = c("Northeast", "Rust Belt", "Sun Belt")),
    hover = paste0(region, "<br>", winner_party, " wins: ", races, " of selected races")
  )

regional_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = regional_results,
  x = ~region,
  y = ~races,
  color = ~winner_party,
  colors = c("Democratic" = "#1d4ed8", "Republican" = "#b91c1c"),
  type = "bar",
  text = ~hover,
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    barmode = "stack",
    xaxis = list(title = NULL),
    yaxis = list(title = "Selected Senate races won", dtick = 1),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12),
    margin = list(t = 30, b = 45)
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

regional_plot
```

CBS News projected Democratic wins in Maine (Troy Jackson), North Carolina (Roy Cooper), Michigan (Abdul El-Sayed), Ohio (Sherrod Brown), Georgia (Jon Ossoff), New Hampshire (Chris Pappas), and Texas (James Talarico). Republican Ashley Moody held Florida. See the [CBS results overview](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/2026-midterm-election-results-where-democrats-won/) and [Senate results page](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/senate-election-results-2026/).

## Political advertising: cycle-level context

Race-level candidate fundraising, independent expenditures, and vote shares are reported through different systems and periods. The comparable total available here is **political advertising**, not all campaign or outside spending. AdImpact estimates reported by Deadline put 2026 cycle ad spending at $12.06 billion, versus $11.2 billion in 2024. The two-cycle comparison is context, not evidence that spending caused a result.

```{r}
#| label: ad-spending
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

ad_spending <- tribble(
  ~cycle, ~spending, ~source_date,
  "2024 presidential cycle", 11.2, "Reported 2026",
  "2026 midterm cycle", 12.06, "Reported Nov. 2026"
) |>
  mutate(
    hover = paste0(cycle, "<br>Estimated political ad spending: $",
                   spending, " billion<br>AdImpact estimate")
  )

ad_spending_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = ad_spending,
  x = ~cycle,
  y = ~spending,
  type = "bar",
  marker = list(color = c("#64748b", "#1d4ed8")),
  text = ~hover,
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = NULL),
    yaxis = list(title = "Estimated political advertising ($ billions)", rangemode = "tozero"),
    margin = list(t = 20, b = 55)
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

ad_spending_plot
```

::: {.source-note}
Source: [Deadline, “Political Ad Spending On 2025–26 Cycle Topped $12 Billion”](https://deadline.com/2026/11/midterm-ad-spending-record-1237226451/), citing AdImpact. Ad spending is a media-market estimate and is not interchangeable with FEC candidate receipts, disbursements, or independent expenditures.
:::
